title: Why AI Memory Prices Are Exploding: The Silent Silicon War
hook: Right now, the world's most critical semiconductor bottleneck isn't the GPU itself. It is the microscopic memory stacked on top of it. And prices are exploding.

scenes.narration: Over the past two years, spot market prices for enterprise memory have surged by more than two hundred percent. What began as a routine tech cycle has morphed into a historic silicon bottleneck.
scenes.purpose: Hook viewer with the sudden reality of skyrocketing memory prices
scenes.visual_hint: Statistic card showing +280% spot price surge with neon glowing trend curve

scenes.narration: To feed modern AI processors, manufacturers must use High Bandwidth Memory. But here is the catch: producing one gigabyte of HBM takes three times as much physical silicon wafer area as standard DDR5.
scenes.purpose: Explain the 3x silicon penalty of HBM vs standard DDR5
scenes.visual_hint: Comparison breakdown showing 300mm wafer yield difference between DDR5 and HBM3e

scenes.narration: By mid-2024, memory giants SK Hynix and Micron dropped an unprecedented bombshell: their entire production lines were sold out through 2025, with major customer allocations already locked in for 2026.
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate the market sell-out across SK Hynix and Micron
scenes.visual_hint: Timeline of supplier capacity sell-outs from 2024 to 2026

scenes.narration: Even with wafers pressed, chips cannot ship without advanced packaging. TSMC's CoWoS packaging lines are stretched to the limit, with order wait times exceeding fifty-two weeks.
scenes.purpose: Highlight the CoWoS packaging choke point at TSMC
scenes.visual_hint: Diagram of TSMC CoWoS advanced packaging interposer bonding GPU and HBM stacks

scenes.narration: Because memory fabs shifted eighty percent of new investment into AI silicon, standard memory inventories collapsed from sixteen weeks down to three. The AI boom is actively cannibalizing consumer tech.
scenes.purpose: Explain the siphon effect on consumer PCs and smartphones
scenes.visual_hint: Inventory drop animation showing channel buffers plunging from 16 weeks to 3 weeks

scenes.narration: As the industry races toward next-generation HBM4, the memory supercycle is no longer just a supply hiccup. It is the defining economic tollbooth of the entire artificial intelligence revolution.
scenes.purpose: Conclude with the next frontier: HBM4 and the long-term reality
scenes.visual_hint: Kinetic typographic summary of next-generation HBM4 architecture

ending: Subscribe to Tech Explained for deeper investigations into the hardware shaping our digital future.
